sections.name: summary
sections.value: Single phase. Two independent pieces of work that share one gate: (a) flip harness telemetry capture to off-by-default without touching the read path, and (b) build the git-ai collector lifecycle in doctor — pinned download-and-verify, hook installation on our terms, and a health ladder that proves collection from an observed checkpoint rather than daemon liveness.

value.title: Move the capture kill-switch default off the environment variable into settings/code so a shipped harness is OFF by default, AND assert the no-op at all three enforcement points (capture-service, sync-service, housekeeping) on a default install.
Prove the read path is ungated: add a test asserting `telemetry pull` and `telemetry report` still resolve an existing published ref while capture is disabled.
Add the pin manifest as committed data — version tag, one SHA-256 per platform artifact, and `expect_schema_version`. No source change may be required to bump it.
Implement platform resolution for all six published artifacts (macos/linux/windows x x64/arm64) mapping from `process.platform` + `process.arch`.
Implement download-and-verify: fetch to a temp path, hash with Node `crypto`, compare against the manifest, and only then place the binary. No shell-out for hashing on any platform.
Make mismatch fail closed: on a digest mismatch place nothing, leave no partial file, and report both expected and actual digests.
Write git-ai's config (`disable_auto_updates`, `disable_version_checks`) BEFORE the binary is first executed, so their updater cannot re-fetch and re-run install.sh behind the pin.
Install hooks by invoking `install-hooks` directly rather than their `install.sh`, so no shell rc, PATH entry, or symlink on the machine is modified by us.

Implement the trace2 guard per Jordan's ruling: read the global trace2 config before EVERY `install-hooks` call (first install and every re-check). Non-empty -> skip install-hooks entirely, warn naming trace2 as the reason, print manual instructions. Empty -> record the observation and proceed. Never delete a trace2 config.

Implement the SIMPLE doctor health read: pinned binary present and hash-matching, hooks current via `install-hooks --dry-run` (verified non-mutating), daemon reachable via its pid file, and expected note schema version. Deliberately shallow — it does not attempt to prove collection is occurring.
Model 'could not determine' as a distinct verdict state, never rendered as healthy and never folded into 'no data'; keep every doctor verdict warn-only with no blocking exit.
Add the pin regenerate command: fetch every platform artifact for a given version, hash them, and rewrite the manifest. The install path must never write the manifest.
Write the docs/how/ page covering the collector handover: what harness no longer captures, what git-ai captures instead, the pin/upgrade procedure, and the trace2 consent behaviour.
Assert the pinned `expect_schema_version` against a note produced after install, so binary drift and note-format drift are caught by the same review.

Record the collection-proof gap as an explicit open design question in the docs/how/ page and the plan: state that v1 cannot prove the capture chain is intact, name why (working log deleted at commit; `time_ago` is a human string), and state that doctor reports 'could not determine' rather than inferring health.

Split the install into two independent stages so a trace2 block degrades rather than fails: stage 1 places the pinned, verified CLI; stage 2 installs hooks and may be skipped. Report the partial state distinctly.
